title: Jonah runs (Jonah 1)
hookLine: the prophet flees to Tarshish and ends up in the sea

cards: The word of the LORD comes to Jonah, son of Amittai, and it's clear. In the King James words: "Arise, go to Nineveh, that great city, and cry against it." Jonah arises.
That part he does. Then the very next verse: "But Jonah rose up to flee unto Tarshish from the presence of the LORD." Nineveh is one direction.
Tarshish is across the sea, the other way. He walks down to the port of Joppa, finds a ship, pays the fare, and climbs aboard.

teach.h: DOWN TO JOPPA, DOWN INTO THE SHIP.
teach.b: Follow Jonah's feet, and the chapter keeps taking him down. Down to Joppa. Down into the ship.

And when the storm hits, he has already gone down into the sides of the ship, the lowest part, and the King James says "he lay, and was fast asleep." Some readers hear running away as a kind of sinking.
Up on deck, everyone else is awake and terrified. Each sailor cries to his own god. They throw the cargo overboard.
The captain finds Jonah asleep below and shakes him: get up, call on your God. The sailors cast lots, and the lot falls on Jonah. Who are you, they ask, where are you from?

teach.h: THE GOD WHICH HATH MADE THE SEA.
teach.b: His answer lands with a sharp irony: "I am an Hebrew; and I fear the LORD, the God of heaven, which hath made the sea and the dry land." The God he's running from made the very water under the ship.
You can't outrun someone who made the road.

teach.h: THE SAILORS TRY TO SAVE HIM.
teach.b: Then the sailors, who don't share his faith, are the ones who fight to save him. Jonah tells them to throw him into the sea. They don't.
They row hard for land, and can't make it. Only then, praying not to be held guilty, do they cast him in. The sea goes still.
And Jonah, who kept going down, is as far down as a man can go, with the chapter not yet done with him.

how: Jews read the whole book of Jonah as the haftarah at the afternoon service of Yom Kippur.

games.q: the storm won't stop and the lot has fallen on Jonah. you're one of the sailors. what do you do?
o: row hard to bring the ship to land.
games.why: the sailors row hard for land and can't make it. only then, praying, do they cast him into the sea.

practice: Ask yourself, without blame, what you've been sailing away from: an email you haven't opened, a conversation you keep postponing, a doctor's appointment, a call you know you need to make.
Let one come up from the bottom of the ship, and don't solve it; just stop moving away from it for a while, and turn to face it the way you'd face the shore. If you pray, you can bring it before God.
